limitations: Scores measure distance from an early-life healthy baseline, not probability of failure.
Thresholds are percentile cuts of that baseline and are dataset-specific.
FD001 has a single operating condition; FD002/FD004 would need condition normalisation.

benchmark.protocol: 80/20 engine-wise split for model selection, refit on all training units, official test scored once at each unit's final cycle

limitations: RUL is expressed in operating cycles, not calendar time.
Training targets are clipped at 125 cycles.
The band is an empirical residual interval, not a calibrated guarantee.
C-MAPSS is simulated; real assets need condition normalisation and maintenance history.

samples.title: Highest-risk recorded failure
samples.narrative: Predicted failure probability 99.7% is elevated. Strongest model attributions — increased the risk: Rotational speed (1307.00), Process-air temperature delta (7.70), Air temperature (302.50). These are model attributions, not confirmed physical causes.

samples.title: Median-risk recorded failure
samples.narrative: Predicted failure probability 89.9% is elevated. Strongest model attributions — increased the risk: Rotational speed (1317.00), Process-air temperature delta (8.20), Air temperature (301.70); reduced the risk: Tool wear (187.00). These are model attributions, not confirmed physical causes.

samples.title: Lowest-risk healthy record
samples.narrative: Predicted failure probability 0.0% is below the alert threshold. Strongest model attributions — reduced the risk: Tool-wear × torque (overstrain proxy) (130.50), Torque (26.10). These are model attributions, not confirmed physical causes.

explainability.method: Permutation importance (global) and occlusion attribution (local): each feature is replaced by the training median and the change in predicted probability is measured.

calibration.note: Reliability is measured on the held-out split; no post-hoc calibrator is applied.

labels.label: Random failure
labels.note: Only 13 labelled cases in training; a model is not trained or exposed.

failure_modes.method: One-vs-rest RandomForest per labelled failure mode
limitations: Labels come from AI4I's simulated milling process, not from a plant CMMS.
Modes can co-occur; the binary 'machine failure' label is their union.
Modes with fewer than 30 training cases are not modelled, by design.
Attribution describes model behaviour, not proven physical causation.
AI4I's power/overstrain/heat modes are deterministic functions of the recorded channels, so their near-perfect PR-AUC reflects label construction, not field realism.
Occlusion attributions are not additive SHAP values; they are local sensitivity.

validation.protocol: Chronological split inside every engine: first 70% of cycles train, remaining cycles test. Features at cycle t use only data up to t.

limitations: Forecasts are in operating cycles, not calendar time.
C-MAPSS is simulated; real sensors need condition normalisation and maintenance context.
Direct multi-horizon models are trained per horizon; they are not a recursive simulation.
MASE is scaled by the naive one-step error on the training portion of each engine.

scenarios.label: Reactive (run to failure)
scenarios.description: No planned work; every failure is an unplanned stop at full loss.

scenarios.label: Scheduled preventive (service all)
scenarios.description: Service every asset on a fixed interval regardless of condition.

scenarios.label: Predictive (budget-constrained)
scenarios.description: Service the highest expected-benefit assets within budget; monitor the rest.

23 of 100 assets had positive expected benefit.

schema.name: ai4i
schema.citation: S. Matzka, 'Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Predictive Maintenance Applications', PHM Asia Pacific 2020. Dataset via UCI ML Repository.
limitations: Synthetic milling-process simulation, not a real production line.
Rows are independent process steps: no time ordering or machine continuity.
Random failures (RNF, 19 rows) are too rare for reliable modelling.
Failure modes overlap; the Machine failure label is the union of the five modes.

schema.name: cmapss
schema.citation: A. Saxena, K. Goebel, D. Simon, N. Eklund, 'Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Simulation', PHM 2008. NASA PCoE repository.
schema.license_note: NASA Open Data Portal; retain attribution to NASA PCoE.
limitations: Simulated turbofan engines, not a factory asset.
Sensor units are simulated physical quantities; do not mix with other datasets.
FD001 has one operating condition and one fault mode; FD002/FD004 have six conditions, which needs condition normalisation to generalise.
Trajectories end at failure, so RUL targets above the clip horizon are uninformative.
